title: Check yourself: LocalDate, LocalTime, and LocalDateTime

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A webinar's start is stored as `2026-11-20T18:00` in a `LocalDateTime` column. The reminder job turns it into an `Instant` with the zone of the server it runs on, and the job is moved from a server in Europe/Berlin to one in Asia/Singapore. No row is touched. When do the reminders fire now?

options.text: At the same moment as before, since the stored value names a moment and the zone the job applies only changes how it prints
options.says: a LocalDateTime holds no moment: Instant.from refuses it, and the zone applied decides which instant it becomes

options.text: At the same moment as before, since the stored value was written in UTC and the job applies UTC on every server
options.says: a LocalDateTime has no zone or offset at all, UTC included; it is only what a wall clock shows

options.text: At a different moment than before, since the stored value names no zone and the job now applies another zone to it
options.says: a LocalDateTime is a wall-clock reading; the same value in two zones is two instants

options.text: At a different moment than before, since the new server shifts the stored value into its own zone as it reads it
options.says: nothing shifts the value; the same unchanged reading becomes another instant only because another zone is applied to it

origin.section: A LocalDateTime Is a Wall-Clock Reading, and the Same One in Two Zones Is Two Moments

questions.stem: A gym bills members monthly. Its code computes each billing date as `previous.plusMonths(1)`, starting from the joining date. A member joined on 2027-08-31. On which day of December 2027 is the December bill dated?

options.text: On the 30th, since each step adds thirty days to the date before it, and four steps land on the 30th
options.says: plusMonths changes the month field and keeps the day when it can; it doesn't add a number of days

options.text: On the 30th, since September's date keeps no trace of the 31st and each step after it starts from the 30th
options.says: plusMonths clamps 31 August to 30 September, and every chained step after that starts from the 30th

options.text: On the 31st, since four steps of one month land on the same date as one step of four months
options.says: chained month steps drift after a clamp; only plusMonths(4) from the joining date gives 2027-12-31

options.text: On the 31st, since each step goes back to the joining day as soon as a month is long enough for it
options.says: the clamped date doesn't remember the 31st, so chained steps stay on the 30th

origin.section: plusMonths Clamps to a Shorter Month's Last Day, So Step From the First Date

questions.stem: A nightly import reads due dates from a partner's file with `LocalDate.parse(text)`. Tonight one line holds `2027-06-31`. What happens to that line?

options.text: It is stored as 2027-06-30, since parsing moves a day the month lacks to the month's last day
options.says: only plusMonths and its kin clamp; parse refuses the text

options.text: It is stored as 2027-07-01, since parsing carries a day the month lacks over into the next month
options.says: rolling over is what lenient SimpleDateFormat did; LocalDate.parse refuses the text

options.text: It fails later with DateTimeException, since parsing checks only the digits and the date's first use checks the calendar
options.says: the calendar check happens in parse itself; a LocalDate that exists is always a valid date

options.text: It fails at once with DateTimeParseException, since parsing refuses a day that the month doesn't have
options.says: LocalDate.parse uses ISO_LOCAL_DATE with its strict resolver and refuses an impossible date

origin.section: LocalDate.parse and LocalDate.of Refuse Dates That Don't Exist

questions.stem: A month-end report computes its cut-off as `firstOfMonth.withDayOfMonth(31)`. It went live in July 2027 and produced the July and August reports without trouble. What does that line do when the report runs for September 2027?

options.text: It throws DateTimeException, since September has no 31st and withDayOfMonth refuses to set one
options.says: withDayOfMonth refuses a day the month doesn't have; lastDayOfMonth() would give 2027-09-30

options.text: It throws DateTimeException, since withDayOfMonth needs a zone, which a LocalDate lacks, to know September's length
options.says: a LocalDate holds no zone and needs none; withDayOfMonth checks the day against the calendar alone

options.text: It returns 2027-09-30, since withDayOfMonth moves a day September lacks to September's last day
options.says: withDayOfMonth doesn't clamp the way plusMonths does; it throws

options.text: It returns 2027-10-01, since withDayOfMonth carries a day September lacks over into October
options.says: java.time doesn't roll over; withDayOfMonth throws for a day the month lacks

origin.section: The Last Day of a Month Comes From an Adjuster, Not a Day Number

concepts: A LocalDateTime is a wall-clock reading with no zone; the same value converted with two zones gives two instants, and Instant.from refuses it.
LocalDate.parse and LocalDate.of refuse a date the calendar doesn't have, and parse also refuses single-digit fields and trailing text; nothing clamps or rolls over.
withDayOfMonth sets the day and throws DateTimeException for a day the month doesn't have, rather than clamping.
